title: Why your recorded voice sounds wrong
description: Your microphone is not playing a trick on you. Here is why your recorded voice sounds different from the voice inside your head. An original illustrated science explainer with synthetic narration.
sources: Background reading (not fetched in this restricted environment): https://www.nidcd.nih.gov/health/how-do-we-hear
Background reading (not fetched in this restricted environment): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voice_confrontation

scenes.heading: Your voice sounds wrong?
scenes.label: There is a reason.
scenes.text: Hate your voice on recordings? Your microphone probably is not the problem.

scenes.heading: You hear two paths.
scenes.label: AIR + VIBRATION
scenes.text: When you speak, sound reaches your ears in two different ways.

scenes.heading: First: through the air.
scenes.label: The path a microphone captures.
scenes.text: One path travels through the air. Your microphone captures sound from this path.

scenes.heading: Second: through your head.
scenes.label: BONE CONDUCTION
scenes.text: Another path carries vibrations through the tissues and bones of your head.

scenes.heading: A different balance.
scenes.label: Your inner listening mix.
scenes.text: This changes the balance of frequencies you hear while you are speaking.

scenes.heading: More depth. More resonance.
scenes.label: Especially in the lower frequencies.
scenes.text: That extra pathway often makes your own voice seem deeper and more resonant.

scenes.heading: The recording is different.
scenes.label: It leaves out that inner pathway.
scenes.text: Play a recording, and you lose that familiar internal contribution. The result can sound surprisingly thin.

scenes.heading: Others hear another mix.
scenes.label: Similar to the recording. Never identical.
scenes.text: Other people hear something closer to the recording. But microphones, rooms, and speakers also change the sound.

scenes.heading: Different is not worse.
scenes.label: Unfamiliar does not mean bad.
scenes.text: An unfamiliar voice is not automatically a bad voice. It is simply different from your everyday experience.

scenes.heading: Try this next time.
scenes.label: Record. Listen. Repeat.
scenes.text: Try recording a short sentence and listening again later. Notice the difference without judging it.

scenes.heading: Your brain knows one version.
scenes.label: The microphone captures another.
scenes.text: Your brain is used to one version of you. A microphone lets you hear another.
